pageContent: Ragen supports multiple LLM providers including OpenAI (GPT-4o, GPT-4-turbo), Anthropic (Claude Sonnet, Claude Haiku), Google (Gemini Flash, Gemini Pro), Amazon Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, Fireworks AI, OpenRouter, and local models via Ollama.

To upload documents, navigate to the Documents section in your project. Supported file formats include PDF, EPUB, Markdown (.md), SRT subtitles, and web URLs. Documents are processed asynchronously through a Temporal workflow pipeline: upload to S3, parse content, generate embeddings, and store in Qdrant.

Ragen uses a hybrid search approach combining BM25 sparse keyword search and dense vector similarity search, fused server-side by Qdrant. Each organization gets its own isolated vector collection. Embeddings are generated using the bge-multilingual-gemma2 model with 3584 dimensions.

Projects allow you to organize assistants and documents within your organization. Each project can have its own set of assistants, document collections, and API keys. Project-level instructions are appended to the system prompt of every assistant in that project.

Assistants can be customized with system prompts (answer instructions) that define their behavior and personality. You can set instructions at the organization level, project level, or per-assistant. Assistant-level instructions take precedence over project-level instructions.

The API is available at /api/v1/ and uses API key authentication via the Authorization: Bearer header. You can create API keys in the organization settings. Each API key is scoped to a specific project and grants access to threads, assistants, documents, and query endpoints.

Ragen pricing includes a free tier with limited messages and document uploads. Paid plans offer higher limits, priority processing, and advanced features like custom model selection and dedicated support. Usage is tracked per organization.

Thread documents allow users to upload files directly in a chat conversation. These documents are processed and made available for retrieval within that specific thread. The assistant can reference both project-level knowledge base documents and thread-specific uploads when answering questions.
